bib.title: Learning towards conversational AI: A survey

read.skipped: Reference list (from offset 94709) skimmed up to Gao et al. 2020 for lineage only.

question: What are the main frameworks and goals of neural open-domain dialogue systems, and how do representative methods, metrics and datasets fit them?
hypothesis: A human-like conversation system should be both informative (knowledge-grounded) and controllable.
contributions: Divide prevailing open-domain dialogue frameworks into retrieval-based, generation-based and hybrid.
Summarize the goals as informative and controllable and review methods for each.
Review evaluation metrics and list corpora and benchmarks.

limits: Authors say the selection follows their own perspective and is by no means complete.
Covers open-domain dialogue only; task-oriented dialogue is mentioned as contrast and QA is not a category.
Pre-LLM (2022): no ChatGPT-style instruction-tuned or tool-using agents; largest model discussed is Meena 2.6B.
Table 1 numbers are collected from original papers, not re-run, and several BERT rows lack Douban results.
Video-grounded dialogue left to future work.
practices: Ground the dialogue in external knowledge (documents, graph, persona, image) to avoid safe/bland responses (Sec 4).
Use hybrid retrieve-then-generate to combine fluent retrieved candidates with novel generation (Sec 3.3).
Warm up RL with MLE before policy gradient; prefer policy gradient over Q-learning for text generation (Sec 3.2.3).
Combine automatic metrics with human evaluation since automatic metrics correlate weakly with human judgment (Sec 6).
Open challenges: logical consistency, interpretability and controllability, efficiency and compactness (Sec 8).

terms.definition: a score function s() and encoding function e() pick the best response from a candidate pool; split into shallow interaction (representation-based) and deep interaction (matching during encoding)
encoder-decoder produces the response token by token; sub-families HRED, VAE, RL, GAN, pre-trained LM
two stage: retrieve similar instances, then use them as prototypes/skeletons for the generator
goal 1: ground dialogue in external knowledge: unstructured text, knowledge graph, persona, visual
goal 2: control dialogue strategy, style, emotion and structure
slot-filling, scenario-specific system for tasks like hotel booking; response confined to limited hypothesis space (used only as contrast)
no explicit limit on topic, larger hypothesis space, goal is communication and companionship
session is a complete dialogue case; single-turn is one query and response; multi-turn has more than one; dyadic has two interlocutors, otherwise multi-party
dialogue where external resources are knowledge documents, graphs, or Wikipedia sentences
